notes: Post-fix evidence for issue #80: every named table target now reaches ddl.table.denylist.forbid regardless of position.

Rework evidence: the earlier 'unqualified destination inherits the source schema' claim was wrong. Per MySQL PT_alter_table_rename (parse_tree_nodes.cc) + LEX::copy_db_to (sql_lex.cc), TiDB handleTableName (preprocess.go), and MySQL bug #11493, an unqualified destination resolves to the current database. Offline CLI audit has no current schema, so qualified_tables selectors cannot match unqualified destinations; the SDK Request.Schema path covers the resolved case.
Probes re-ran against the reworked working tree; ids renamed where the old id encoded the wrong claim (see *_dest_unqualified).
IDs mysql.denylist_*/tidb.denylist_* re-run the same inputs as the pre-fix 2026-09-21 probe file for direct comparison.

Extended ids cover RENAME destinations, ALTER TABLE ... RENAME TO destinations, unqualified destinations under qualified_tables (unknown-schema boundary offline), schema-qualified and quoted identifiers, dotted qualified identities that must not deduplicate, and all-allowed controls.
Synthetic offline audit probes only; submitted SQL was never executed against a database.
--fail-on none avoids conflating finding thresholds with verdict; inspect diagnostics and exit_code separately.
